title: The Evolution of Analytical Metrology for High Spatial Resolution and Sensitivity in the Analytical Transmission Electron Microscope
content: Since the earliest use of microscopes as tools for the characterization of materials [1-9], the roles and capabilities of these instruments for characterization have continuously evolved. Using electron optical instrumentation in the 1960’s – 70’s, materials analysts using the transmission electron microscope concentrated upon experiments [10-12] which are generally based on elastic scattering events. These imaging and diffraction studies were used to investigate microstructure, phases, intrinsic and extrinsic defects, dislocations, as well as characterize the changes during environmental events, resulting from a range of sources including deformation, irradiation, as well as in-situ events such as heating/cooling [13-16].
